paragraphs.source_en: “A sign of opulence,” retorted Laigle calmly. “I congratulate you. You have there a rent of nine thousand francs per annum.” At that moment, Courfeyrac emerged from the café. Marius smiled sadly. “I have paid this rent for the last two hours, and I aspire to get rid of it; but there is a sort of history attached to it, and I don’t know where to go.” “Come to my place, sir,” said Courfeyrac. “I have the priority,” observed Laigle, “but I have no home.” “Hold your tongue, Bossuet,” said Courfeyrac. “Bossuet,” said Marius, “but I thought that your name was Laigle.” “De Meaux,” replied Laigle; “by metaphor, Bossuet.” Courfeyrac entered the cab. “Coachman,” said he, “hotel de la Porte-Saint-Jacques.” And that very evening, Marius found himself installed in a chamber of the hotel de la Porte-Saint-Jacques side by side with Courfeyrac.
